title: Log the fridge thermometer's maximum before resetting it
instruction: Reset the vaccine fridge's thermometer for the day and log this morning's maximum on the board.
context: Done by: pharmacy technicians and medical assistants (O*NET 29-2052, 31-9092). Each workday they log the fridge's max/min, then reset it (CDC Vaccine Storage Toolkit). Reset first and a warm overnight excursion, which must be reported, is lost. The order is not stated; a vial carton is a distractor. Unlike TK-WZKR6E (reset a peak-flow marker), TK-29RHVG and TK-D7MBTK (read and log a value), the reading here is destroyed by a step the task requires.
setup: Directions are from the robot's view: 'out' is away from the arm bases, left and right are the robot's, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. The table stands for the top of a vaccine fridge. Thermometer unit (fixed, plastic): a dark grey slab 120 mm out-to-back, 190 mm wide and 20 mm tall, centred 32 cm out and 10 cm left of the midline. On its far half (centre line 30 mm beyond the slab's centre) lies a scale of five colour bands, each 28 mm wide and 28 mm deep: blue, green, yellow, orange, red, left to right, the blue band's left edge 70 mm left of the slab's centre. On the slab's out-to-back centre line runs a white track 24 mm deep and 135 mm long, its middle 7.5 mm right of the slab's centre. On it: a grey index (20 x 5 x 6 mm, the present temperature) 39.5 mm left of the slab's centre, inside the green band; and a black plastic stored-maximum marker (18 x 18 x 10 mm, 20 g) to the index's right, held where it stands by a spring. A white RESET button (24 mm across, 12 mm tall) stands 40 mm nearer the robot than the slab's centre; pressed 5 mm down (of 8 mm travel) it returns the marker to the index (centre 28 mm left of the slab's centre, the middle of the green band) for the rest of the trial. Log board (fixed, plastic): a light grey slab 70 mm out-to-back, 200 mm wide and 15 mm tall, centred 37 cm out and 14 cm right of the midline. On its far half (34 mm deep, centre line 12 mm beyond the board's centre): a white blank zone 34 mm wide at the left end (from 90 to 56 mm left of the board's centre), then the same five bands, 28 mm each, left to right. A black plastic pointer tab (18 mm out-to-back, 14 mm wide, 25 mm tall, 30 g) stands on a grey rail 20 mm nearer the robot than the board's centre and slides left and right along it; it starts centred in the blank zone (73 mm left of the board's centre). A white cardboard vial carton (60 x 40 x 30 mm, 0.1 kg) lies 45 cm out and 27 cm left; it is a distractor and plays no part in scoring. Lots: the marker starts with its centre at the middle of the yellow band (lot A), the red band (lot B) or the orange band (lot C). Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial. Score 0 for the whole trial if at any point RESET is pressed (5 mm or more down; the marker visibly jumps back to the index) while the pointer tab's centre is not in the band the marker stood in at the start (the morning's maximum); judged from the video. Otherwise, at the end, with no gripper or fingertip within 5 mm of the pointer tab, marker or button and all three still: 1.0 if the pointer tab's centre is within that band (its full 28 mm, edges included) and the marker is reset (a gap of at most 3 mm between the marker and the index); 0.5 if the pointer is in that band and the marker is not reset; 0 otherwise (pointer in any other band or still in the blank zone). Possible scores 0, 0.5, 1.0. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Slide the pointer tab back to the middle of the blank zone and let the RESET button up. Set the marker for the lot: centred on the yellow (A), red (B) or orange (C) band. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: An analogue max/min thermometer standing in for a vaccine fridge's digital data logger, and five colour bands in place of degree marks; the log is a sliding pointer, not a written entry. The marker is held by a spring and moved by the reset only; a hand push springs back. Parts are rigid; masses and friction are simulator values. The three lots stop a fixed habit (always green, always the top), not a memorised replay of all three layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in lots A and B (lot C's trial was refused by the Dream-1 service and not scored); demo: 1.0 in each lot
